lecture_script: Hello, everyone! Today, we'll explore how tiny microbes help us in big ways. Let's dive into the world of microbes in industrial products. First, we'll talk about antibiotics. Antibiotics are medicines that kill or stop bacteria. One famous antibiotic is penicillin. Penicillin was discovered by Alexander Fleming. He noticed that a mold killed bacteria around it. This mold made penicillin. It is used to treat many bacterial infections. Now, let's move to organic acids. These are acids made by living things. Two important organic acids are citric acid and acetic acid. Citric acid is found in citrus fruits like lemons. It is used in food and drinks for a sour taste. Acetic acid is what makes vinegar sour. It is used in cooking and preserving food. Next, let's discuss enzymes. Enzymes are proteins that speed up reactions. Two common enzymes are lipase and pectinase. Lipase breaks down fats. It is used in detergents to clean oily stains. Pectinase breaks down pectin, which is in fruits. It is used to make fruit juices clear. Now, let's talk about bioactive molecules. These are chemicals that affect living things. Two important bioactive molecules are cyclosporin A and statins. Cyclosporin A is used in medicine to help organ transplants. It stops the body from rejecting the new organ. Statins are used to lower cholesterol in the blood. They help prevent heart diseases. In industry, we use a special machine called a fermenter. A fermenter is a big tank where microbes grow and make products. After this, we have downstream processing. This is the step where we clean and purify the product. Let's look at an industrial fermenter. It has a big tank with pipes and controls. It keeps the right temperature and air for microbes to grow. Remember, microbes are used in many industries. They make medicines, food, and even clean products. A common mistake is thinking all microbes are harmful. But many are helpful! To sum up, microbes are tiny but mighty. They help us make important products. Understanding this is key for NEET exams. Keep these points in mind, and you'll do great!

definitions.definition: Medicines that kill or stop the growth of bacteria.
Acids made by living organisms, such as citric acid and acetic acid.
Proteins that speed up chemical reactions.
Chemicals that affect living organisms, like cyclosporin A and statins.
A large tank used in industry to grow microbes and produce products.
The step where products are cleaned and purified after production.
